about: Request to turn the disarmer towards the trap, created by esv::trap::DisarmSystem::ProcessDisarmRequests (bg3.exe+0x2CF5BC0 lines 288-317) and consumed by esv::steering::StateSystem::Update (macOS signature lists it next to esv::lock::SteeringRequestOneFrameComponent; game reader bg3.exe+0x302CB80). Creator bg3.exe+0x2CF9C70 (AllocRaw 0x30). Same creator defaults and writer pattern as esv::lock::SteeringRequestOneFrameComponent (layouts/dead) - field names follow that twin. Not saved.

evidence.says: Creator zeroes +0..+0xC; writer line 291-296: dwords +0/+4 = request element +0x10 (the trap item). First alternative storage of a target variant (entity or direction), as in the lock twin.
Writer stores 0 as a 32-bit value at +8; third dword of the variant storage.
Writer stores dword 1 at +0xC (the fourth dword) - variant index 1 = entity, as in the lock twin.
Creator writes dword 0 at +0x10; not written by the trap writer. Name as in the lock twin (copied into the steering state).

Creator zeroes +0x18/+0x20; writer lines 306-313 store a new Guid (bg3.exe+0x4130D80) and copy it into DisarmingStateComponent.SteeringTransactionId (lines 315-317); bg3.exe+0x2CF6EF0 compares the steering state's Guid with it.
Creator writes 0x4B18967F (9999999.0); writer sets 1.0 (writes 0x3F800000 as a 32-bit value at +0x28). Same as the lock twin (copied into esv::steering::LifetimeComponent).
